source_title: Actress Kate Miller Recalls Being Starstruck by ‘Meticulous’ Bob Mackie - People.com
source_excerpt:
Miller shares her profound admiration for the late designer
Kate Miller/Instagram; Angela Weiss/Getty
Katie Miller worked with Carol Burnett and Bob Mackie in the Broadway production of Moon Over Buffalo
Miller says Bob Mackie’s meticulous approach made her especially nervous during costume fittings
The designer created many of Burnett’s most memorable costumes for her longtime comedy series
Broadway actress Katie Miller says there was someone who was even more intimidating than former costar and comedy icon Carol Burnett : the late designer Bob Mackie.
In an interview on The Jim Masters Show , Miller, 57, spoke about working with the legendary costume designer on the Broadway production of Moon Over Buffalo , in which she played the role of Eileen and Burnett played the lead role of Charlotte Hay.
“I was more starstruck in my fittings [by Mackie] than I was sometimes by Carol,” she said. “He’s just soft-spoken and and fastidious and meticulous and a gentleman and fabulous. Just a great energy and just a genius.”

She continued: “I mean, what what do you say? We see it all the time. We’ve seen his clothes forever — we’ve seen his costumes, his wardrobe, his sequin gowns, all of it.”
“That was fun, hearing all the stories backstage about The Carol Burnette Show that she would, she goes, ‘Well, that was Bob’s idea.’ ... that’s how Bob Mackie is. He wasn’t just an amazing, glamorous designer. He was a whole other animal,” she added.
Mackie died at the age of 87 in Palm Springs, Calif., from pneumonia , a rep confirmed to PEOPLE.

In a post shared on Mackie’s Instagram page on Sept. 14, his team wrote, “It is with a heavy heart that we share the news that Mr. Bob Mackie passed away today. He lived his 87 years to the fullest, fulfilling his dream of being a Fashion and Costume Designer, which is all he ever wanted to do. His genius and extraordinary designs will live on forever, continuing to bring beauty into this world.”
